_what: What stands on each place's own ground: who lives there and how many, how the houses sit, what lies outside the town, and every feature the place's own words describe. The local map draws from this instead of guessing from the place's kind. Read with local_layouts.json: an authored layout's named sites stay as they are; this file adds the dwellings, the outlying farms and the unnamed features, and never a second copy of a named site.
_erik: Erik, 2026-10-08: "most of the local maps are too simple and are in error at times. Not every location had homes... and if they do they aren't always lined neatly along the roads. In some places, you're supposed to have shrines and temples but they're not necessarily on the map. The spent yard doesn't show the machinery and reclamation process at all. if there are towns, such as millbrook you should also see farm houses and things of that sort scattered around the area."
_source: Every entry is read off the place's own appearance and description lines; `_why` quotes the line it came from. Nothing here is invented that the place's words do not say, except the count of farmsteads around a farming settlement, which its fields imply.

dwellings.none: nobody lives here: no roofs at all; any buildings are the features listed
dwellings.city: 150 or more, as many as the frame can show

layout.cluster: irregular knots round the centre and the junctions, at varied angles and spacing, with yards and gaps between; thinning outward; never two even rows down a road
layout.street: strung along one line (the road, the stream or the rim the entry names), with a little depth behind the frontage
layout.rings: concentric rings, evenly spaced, streets running out radially
layout.tiers: stepped levels, up a slope or down round a shaft or a lake
layout.stilts: on piles over water, linked by walks; no ground under them
layout.rock: backed hard against a rock face or into a cavern mouth, stepping up it
layout.dug: cut into the rock: doorways and openings in a face, not roofs
layout.canopy: in or grown from trees, among the wood rather than cleared from it
layout.scatter: few buildings, far apart, open ground between
layout.yard: buildings round an open yard, facing in
layout.court: buildings round a court or garden on three or four sides
layout.camp: tents or wagons in a loose curve, fires between
layout.hulls: boats lashed together on the water
layout.floating: on a floating island or above the ground; the ground below shows through
layout.underwater: under the surface: drawn through the water
layout.interior: a room or a run of rooms: the map is a plan of the inside

at.centre: the middle of the place, where its mark is
at.road: beside a road out, near the built edge
at.along: repeated along the main road or the line the entry names
at.water: at the shore or in the water
at.edge: on the outskirts, in the clear between the roads
at.across: a line through the whole frame
at.end: at one end of the site
at.scatter: spread far apart over the whole ground
at.junctions: at each junction of the streets

_rules.state: abandoned (dimmed, roofs fallen) · ruined · unfinished (outline, scaffold) · dead (grey, leafless) · sealed · empty · fouled · razed (footprint only) · former (faint marks of an old layout)
_rules.effects: doubled (every mark faintly drawn twice, offset) · false_fronts (buildings as facades with nothing behind) · frames (buildings drawn as open frames) · roofless · unlit (the map is dark but for what is lit) · stopped (nothing on the map animates) · scorched (dark arcs on the faces toward the light) · rain (streaks over everything) · blocky (all ground squared off to a grid) · shifting (the marks of other layouts show faintly)
_rules.own: the feature that IS the place: drawn at the place's own mark, the first thing the eye finds
_rules.farms: A surface village, town or city (layout cluster, street, rows, grid or court) is ringed by its farmland, with farmsteads scattered in it — a farmhouse with its barn and yard, each on a short track off the nearest road, never in a row: village 4–8, town 8–14, city 12–20, unless the entry says `farms: false` (its own words rule farmland out) or gives `outlying` itself. Hamlets and everything else farm only where the entry says so.

_kinds._marks: drawn: an existing glyph in engine/mapicons.mjs, or `new` where nothing fits yet

gate.what: a gate arch, a waygate, a great door

hall.what: a hall, a long building, a barracks, a bathhouse, a gatehouse, a chamber

shrine.what: a small shrine (drawn smaller than a temple)

cairn_row.what: a line of cairns along a way: `n` cairns

stone_field.what: many small upright stones in loose rows

tower.what: a tower, a spire of a city, a clock tower

wall.what: a wall (a ring wall with `at: ring`, a line with `at: across`)

cistern.what: a cistern, a basin, a pool

square.what: an open paved square or plaza

market.what: a market stall or a lane of stalls

machinery.what: machinery standing in the open: gears, housings, engines

crane.what: a crane, hoist, gantry, rig or scaffold

stacks.what: sorted material stacked in rows: salvage, lumber, stone, records

boats.what: boats moored or drawn up: `n` hulls

post.what: a post, pillar, stake, lamp-pole or marker

lens.what: a mounted lens or mirror rig

stair.what: a great stair or flight of steps

cave.what: a cave mouth, shaft, cell, tunnel or opening down

farmstead.what: a farmhouse with its barn and yard

footings.what: the footprint of a building that is no longer there

figure.what: a great carved symbol standing in the open

aperture.what: a round opening in a wall, capped

leviathan.what: a leviathan's back breaking the water, huts on it

solid.what: a geometric solid with no way in

sun_disc.what: a kept sun in a cavern roof, ringed with machinery

column.what: a column of people and carts on the move

stream.what: a stream, drawn as narrow water

hedgerow.what: a hedge along a field edge

rock.what: bare rock, scree, a rock face

water.what: open water: a pool, a lake, the sea

blocks.what: ground resolved into stacked square units

features._note: roofed stalls with written boards along the descending gallery
lamps at fixed intervals

the_low_market._why: An orderly market of roofed stalls along a descending stone gallery, each with a written board hung above it. Lamps at fixed intervals.

features._note: the vast opening the city descends into
walkways spiralling the walls

the_maw._why: A city built downward into a vast opening — tiers of dark buildings descending around the shaft, walkways spiralling the walls.

features._note: workshops beside the road
pump-houses
the waygate arch
long pipe runs leaving in both directions
spare parts crated

the_measured_engine._why: An outpost of workshops and pump-houses beside a road, with a waygate arch at one end and long pipe runs leaving in both directions.

features._note: the broad low building, doors kept open
the inner court
water basins

the_mercy_house._why: A broad low building of pale stone with wide doors kept open, colonnaded walks around an inner court. Water basins.

features._note: cairns marking the line of the road
drystone shelters set against the rock

the_mountain_pass._why: A long stone-floored saddle between peaks, with drystone shelters set against the rock and cairns marking the line of the road.

features._note: the unmarked stone
the one open arch

the_null_stone._why: A block of unmarked grey stone at the centre of the Crossing's hub, where five arches ring it — four sealed, one open.

features._note: empty halls of pale stone, lit and swept

the_numen._why: Empty halls of pale stone, lit and swept, containing nothing at all — no furniture, no occupants visible.

features._note: the stone watch-post and its square corner tower
the fold of ground sheltering it from the north

the_old_warden_post._why: A small stone watch-post on a shoulder of open ground — three rooms and a stair, a square corner tower. Heath around it, the road below.

features._note: rows of dead fruit trees in perfect order
the dead sun in the cavern roof, ringed with machinery

the_orchard_gone_out._why: Rows of dead fruit trees in perfect order, reaching up toward a dead sun: a great dark disc ringed with machinery in the cavern roof.

features._note: the flat shelf of rock
the rail along the shelf edge, the valley below

the_painters_shelf._why: A one-room cabin of silvered timber on a flat shelf of rock, a plank porch facing out over the drop. A single cabin, not a village.

features._note: cased shelving, bound volumes behind glass

the_proof_halls._why: A long vaulted stone hall lined with cased shelving from floor to ceiling.

features._note: the waygate, grown around rather than cut for

the_quickwood_eaves._why: Where shaped living trunks give way to ordinary forest — buildings becoming trees by degrees. A waygate stands among the eaves-trees.

features._note: low buildings with wide windows and broad verandas
still grey pools
open lawns

the_quiet_ground._why: Low buildings with unusually wide windows set among still grey pools, spaced far apart on open lawns. More empty ground than built.

features._note: the single wide building with an entrance on every side
level swept ground; no walls, no gate

the_quiet_house._why: A single wide stone building with an entrance on every side, set alone on level swept ground. No walls, no gate, no guard post.

features._note: the low concrete-and-lattice structure half-sunk in the riverbed
pale seamless housings in ordered ranks, lit from within
the water led through the housings in open channels
the intake grilles along its river face

the_reclamation_site._why: A low concrete-and-lattice structure half-sunk in the riverbed, intake grilles along its whole river face. Inside, pale seamless housings in ordered ranks, the water led through them in open channels.

features._note: sanded duelling circles set into paved squares
training grounds
barracks halls behind

the_redline._why: A city of training grounds and duelling floors — sanded circles set into paved squares, banked seating around the larger rings. Barracks halls behind.

features._note: the river running black and fast through the floor's channel
nine round apertures, each capped flush

the_regulator_chamber._why: A vault of fitted pale stone; the floor slopes to a channel where the river runs black and fast. Nine round apertures around the wall, each capped flush.

features._note: white salt-pans in square rows
boats tied up where streets would be
nets drying on every rail

the_saltmarch._why: Houses on stilts over grey shallows, white salt-pans in square rows, nets drying on every rail, and boats tied up where streets would be.

features._note: swept down to bare stone
ash-marked stakes where things were built and removed
the city's demolition-towers a mile off

the_scour_gate_yard._why: A wide space swept down to bare stone round the gate arch, nothing standing on it. Ash-marked stakes show where things were once built and deliberately removed.

features._note: the footings of a city, lines in the dirt

the_scouring._why: Flat cleared ground where a city was, the footings still visible as lines in the dirt. Nothing standing above knee height.

features._note: the paved yard with the shared bench
lenses, burners and assay glass
chalk boards and slate racks

the_second_reading._why: Two workshops facing across a paved yard. A shared bench runs between them.

the_service_ways._why: Precursor tunnels running dead straight into the dark (the authored layout carries its ways).

features._note: the long hall of benches under clock-faces

the_slow_hour_gate_yard._why: A long hall of benches under clock-faces that show different hours, the gate arch at the far end.

features._note: old fruit trees in long straight rows
low stone walls between the plots
a path down every row
mown

the_slow_orchard._why: Widely spaced old fruit trees in long straight rows on mown grass. Low stone walls between the plots, and a path down every row.

features._note: the vast stair, long flights and broad landings

the_slow_stair._why: A vast stair cut into rock, climbing for days in long flights and broad landings.

features._note: where loads come in off the road and are sorted
timber, plate, cable and machinery stacked in labelled rows
the unidentifiable machinery among the rows
open sheds
the cutting rigs under the sheds
what is cut away
churned ground

the_spent_yard._order: The reclamation reads as a line from the road: the yard where it comes in, the labelled rows where it waits, the sheds where the rigs cut it down. Nothing whole anywhere.
the_spent_yard._why: A breaking yard of sorted salvage — timber, plate, cable and unidentifiable machinery stacked in labelled rows on churned ground. Cutting rigs under open sheds.

features._note: gardens at every junction

the_stillhold._why: A walled city of pale ordered buildings on a regular plan, gardens at every junction, streets swept and level.

the_stopped._why: A place where nothing moves — dust suspended, people mid-step. Everything is exactly as it was at one instant.

features._note: plain upright stones in loose rows, each with one carved line
no path, no fence

the_told_ground._why: A wide field of plain upright stones set in loose rows, each one carrying a single carved line of text. Grass between them, no path, no fence.

features._note: bare stone, no ornament, no benches, no shade

the_unblinking_stone_gate_yard._why: A bare stone yard with a wall and a gate arch and nothing else.

the_unfallen._why: White buildings burning at the edges with a light that has begun to scorch what stands near them — ground scorched in clean arcs.

features._note: people and carts strung out to the horizon both ways
the ruts behind them

the_unlanded._why: A column of people and carts moving across open country, strung out to the horizon in both directions. No camp, no fires, no halt.

features._note: dwellings cut into the rock, unlit and unmarked

the_unlit_deep._why: Deep caverns with every lamp-niche deliberately emptied and stopped with stone. Dwellings cut into the rock, unlit and unmarked.

features._note: the room that matches nothing around it
the perfect corridor

the_unplanned_room._why: A single room that does not match anything around it, a doorway set at the wrong height in an otherwise perfect corridor.

features._note: frames, lattices and solids with no way in

the_untethered._why: Structures of pure geometry standing in empty space — no doors, no floors and no way in.

features._note: one long stone building, stabling at one end
the lamp on a pole and the board of pinned notes
the waygate in the yard, unfenced

the_wayhouse._why: One long stone building alone at a crossroads, with a lamp on a pole outside. A waygate stands in the yard, unfenced and unwatched.

features._note: the great balance scales, beams the width of a cart
weights racked by size along one wall
the covered assay bench

the_weighing_yard._why: An open stone yard with great balance scales standing in the middle. Weights racked along one wall, a covered assay bench along another.

features._note: water running down every surface

the_wellspring_deep._why: A drowned city under constant weather. Buildings open to it, no roofs. Everything streaming.

features._note: curved wagons and low awnings in a loose curve
fires between
tracks that curve away rather than run straight

the_wend._why: A road-people's camp of curved wagons and low awnings arranged in a loose curve, fires between.

features._note: the cleared and levelled site
the sorted materials of what stood there
the long open shed
rigs, chain and cutting gear under the shed

the_worn_yard._order: Demolition reads end to end: the levelled site at one end, the sorted stacks of it at the other, the rigs under the shed between.
the_worn_yard._why: A demolition yard with a cleared and levelled site at one end and the sorted materials of what stood there stacked at the other. Rigs, chain and cutting gear under a long open shed.

features._note: the light-guide junction under the floor

the-low-lamp-inn._why: A low timber-and-stone inn built over a light-guide junction, so the glow comes up through the floor.

features._note: the shallow stream the town runs along
small shrines, each with a bench facing the water
open-fronted listening-houses
hanging cords and marked posts

thinwater._why: A town of small shrines and open-fronted listening-houses along a shallow stream, each with a bench facing the water. Hanging cords and marked posts between them. Much open ground.

thornwake_glade._why: The few who live at its edge call themselves wardens (the authored layout carries the glade and the Warden Edge).

features._note: the market on the biggest deck that never closes

tidewrought._why: Hundreds of hulls lashed into one floating town, masts like a forest, rope bridges between decks, and a market on the biggest deck.

features._note: the long hall of numbered booths
the numbered booths

tier_seven_gate_yard._why: A clean, bright receiving level, the gate arch at one end of a long hall of numbered booths.

features._note: tents, stalls and improvised frontages at odd angles
the marks of other layouts

tumbledown_market._why: A market of tents, stalls and improvised frontages packed at odd angles, with lanes that do not run straight. The ground shows the marks of other layouts.

features._note: the black lake
stone quays
lamplit boats
the great door at the top of the stair, a lock on each face

undermere._why: A black lake under a cavern roof, stone quays and lamplit boats, a city built in tiers around the water, and a great door at the top of the stair.

features._note: the half-built stone bridge from one bank
the surveyor's line of stakes across the water
masons' sheds
stacked blocks
the road-walkers' camp on the other side

waystone._why: A half-built stone bridge from one bank and a surveyor's line of stakes across the water. Masons' sheds and stacked blocks on one side, a road-walkers' camp on the other.

features._note: the arch standing in the shallows
the broad steps down to the tidal pool
the tidal pool
the first public hall, doors open

wellspring_gate_yard._why: Broad steps down to a tidal pool, the gate arch standing in the shallows. The first of the public halls stands at the top of the steps.

features._note: the spires on the floating crag
chains as thick as a man running down to the anchor-forts
the anchor-forts on the peaks

windspire._why: Spires on a floating crag, chains as thick as a man running down to anchor-forts on the peaks.
